scenario.recruiter: time-constrained independent recruiter managing several relationship contexts
scenario.trigger: A recruiter starts to create a contact whose exact account-scoped name already exists under other relationship contexts.
scenario.job_to_be_done: Add the new recruiter-owned source to the right stable person and relationship without creating a duplicate identity or flattening separate relationships.
scenario.success_condition: The recruiter sees the possible existing person, deliberately chooses an existing or new relationship, receives an accurate operation receipt, and can reload the resulting person-context URL.
scenario.pressure_limit: The synthetic replay has a realistic duplicate-record cost but no measured field time pressure or competing live-search workload.

frozen_evidence: 19 Web test files and 86 tests passing
Database readback: one active person, three active relationship contexts, and four governed sources

findings.observation: Exact-name discovery prevents the common accidental duplicate and makes the relationship choice explicit, but several plausible same-name people still appear as a list rather than a dedicated unresolved identity comparison.
findings.evidence: The live replay showed one possible person, its existing relationships and source count, a disabled distinct-person action, and an explicit New relationship path. No multi-candidate comparison was exercised.
findings.user_impact: The ordinary repeat-contact path is faster, while a genuine same-name collision can still require off-screen reconstruction before the recruiter knows which person to choose.
findings.recommendation: When several plausible people exist, show only stable differentiators backed by confirmed handles or recruiter-owned context and allow leave unresolved without creating either record.
findings.verification: Seed two same-name people with different confirmed handles and contexts; the recruiter can inspect match reasons, leave unresolved, or choose one without an automatic merge.

findings.observation: The executable flow removes duplicate person creation and repeated context entry in the synthetic case, but no working recruiter comparison measures whether it beats search, notes, or ATS fallback under time pressure.
findings.evidence: The browser and database replay is synthetic and local.
findings.user_impact: The product plausibly saves reconciliation work, but the size and frequency of that value are not yet commercial evidence.
findings.recommendation: Run a timed identity-and-context binding comparison with consented recruiter cases.
findings.verification: Measure completion time, duplicate-record rate, wrong-context corrections, abandonment, and willingness to reuse across at least five recruiter-owned cases.

strengths: The default path searches before it creates.
One existing person can hold several purpose-scoped relationships without flattening them.
The recruiter supplies only a name, relationship choice, and one source; no second profile form is required.
The completed receipt names the actual operation instead of using generic AI success language.
Reload preserves the selected person and relationship context.
missing_evidence: Several plausible same-name candidates with confirmed-handle evidence.
Day-later return and persisted Agent operation history.
open_questions: Which two or three source-backed differentiators let recruiters resolve common same-name cases without turning this into a CRM form?

reviews.lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

findings.observation: The Agent now performs account-scoped name narrowing, labels name as a discovery hint rather than proof, never auto-merges, fails closed when lookup is unavailable, and requires explicit confirmation before creating a different same-name person. Confirmed handles and an unresolved multi-candidate case are not yet surfaced in this UI.
findings.evidence: agent-person-resolution.ts; five identity-resolution tests plus one three-outcome receipt test; browser replay; database readback with one person across three contexts.
findings.user_impact: The corrected path prevents silent duplicate creation in the proven exact-name case. A recruiter can still choose the wrong candidate when names collide and no distinguishing evidence is visible.
findings.recommendation: Add source-linked confirmed-handle match reasons and a leave-unresolved identity case before widening autonomous intake.
findings.verification: Exercise two same-name people, an exact confirmed handle, lookup failure, cancel, retry, and later correction; no branch may auto-merge or publish person state before review.

findings.observation: The person, contexts, and sources survive reload, while the completed Agent operation receipt remains transient UI state.
findings.evidence: The Advisor network URL restored the original person and new relationship after reload; the Relationship context added card did not persist.
findings.user_impact: Evidence truth is preserved, but a returning recruiter cannot audit whether the new context came from this Agent operation without consulting lower-level history.
findings.recommendation: Persist a compact purpose-scoped operation event separately from candidate facts and generated Chat prose.
findings.verification: Create, reuse, cancel, reload, and delete; the operation history preserves actor, object, outcome, and idempotency without becoming evidence about the person.

strengths: Name matching narrows choices but carries no merge authority.
New-person creation fails closed when the account lookup is unavailable.
The same stable person identifier is preserved when a new relationship context is added.
Source intake remains purpose-scoped and recruiter-owned.
No external message, calendar, contact, ATS, or CRM write is authorized by this flow.
The UI and database readback agree on the completed identity outcome.
missing_evidence: Confirmed-handle match reasons in the Agent surface.
Multi-candidate unresolved identity review and later correction.
open_questions: Which confirmed identity handles may be displayed safely, and which should be masked while still explaining the match?

affected_finding_result.prior_finding: The Agent contact form did not show same-name or confirmed-handle candidates before creation.
